analyzed_vuln.description: xmlLoadEntityContent grows the external entity's xmlBuf while the active xmlParserInput still caches base/cur/end pointers into that buffer. A successful xmlBufGrow realloc can free the cached allocation. If a later grow fails, xmlBufResetInput is called with buf->error set and returns without refreshing those pointers; xmlLoadEntityContent then calls xmlFatalErr while ctxt->input still contains the dangling pointers. Error reporting reaches xmlParserPrintFileContextInternal and reads input->cur, causing the heap-use-after-free. The root cause is failure-path pointer synchronization in xmlLoadEntityContent, not the context-printing read.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The parser must load an external parsed entity (in this PoV, an external parameter entity referenced while decoding an entity value, with entity substitution/validation behavior causing xmlLoadEntityContent to run). Its content must be large enough that xmlParserInputBufferGrow successfully reallocates the backing xmlBuf, and allocation fault injection or real OOM must make a subsequent grow fail. The failing grow sets buf->error; xmlBufResetInput therefore refuses to update input->base/cur/end, and the immediately raised fatal error dereferences the stale pre-reallocation parser-input pointers.

args: Analyze the failure-path pointer synchronization bug in `xmlLoadEntityContent` in `libxml2/parser.c` around line 8200. What is the safest minimal root-cause fix when `xmlParserInputBufferGrow` reallocates `input->buf->buffer`, and a later grow fails leaving `buf->error` set so `xmlBufResetInput` refuses to refresh `input->base/cur/end`? Consider whether synchronization should happen after every successful grow, whether offsets must be preserved, and whether changing `xmlBufResetInput` globally would be unsafe.

The provided ASan report shows a heap-use-after-free during error reporting: `xmlLoadEntityContent` repeatedly grows an external entity input buffer; an earlier successful realloc frees the allocation cached by active `xmlParserInput` pointers, then a later allocation-injected grow failure sets the xmlBuf error. The function calls `xmlBufResetInput`, but that helper returns early when the buffer has an error, then calls `xmlFatalErr`, whose context printer reads stale `input->cur`.
